title: Can one shy person stop a riot?
hook: Two crowds of 100 differ in one person's nerve. Do they behave almost the same?

knows: people join once enough others have
doesNotKnow: that a crowd's outcome can hinge on one person's threshold, not on the crowd's average mood

misconception: Two crowds with almost identical people behave almost identically.
objective: The learner can explain that with thresholds 0, 1, ..., 99 each joiner brings the count to the next person's threshold, so all 100 join; changing the single threshold of 1 to 2 leaves no one who joins at a count of 1, so only the first mover joins, though the average threshold moves only from 49.5 to 49.51.

claims.text: With thresholds 0, 1, 2, ..., 99 and everyone seeing everyone, all 100 people join, one more each round.
claims.source: Builder's node run 2026-10-14 (synchronous rounds, person joins when joined count >= threshold): 100 join; in round r exactly the person with threshold r - 1 joins, 100 rounds. Same joinRounds() as Demo.tsx. | FC pass 22 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): own copy of joinRounds() (scratchpad fc22/riot.mjs): 100 join, person i joins in round i+1, 100 rounds.

claims.text: Changing the single threshold of 1 to 2 leaves only 1 person joining: after the first mover, everyone left needs at least 2 others.
claims.source: Builder's node run 2026-10-14: thresholds 0, 2, 2, 3, ..., 99 stop at 1. After round 1 the count is 1 and the smallest remaining threshold is 2. | FC pass 22 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): same script with threshold of person 1 set to 2: 1 joins.

claims.text: The change moves the average threshold only from 49.5 to 49.51.
claims.source: Sum 0..99 = 4950, mean 49.5; raising one value by 1 gives 4951 / 100 = 49.51. | FC pass 22 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): 4950/100 = 49.5; 4951/100 = 49.51 (node); readout uses mean().toFixed(2).

claims.text: A chain like this needs a next person at every count, so one missing link stops it.
claims.source: With joined count k, the process continues only if some non-joiner has threshold <= k. Node check 2026-10-14: raising any single threshold j to j + 1 in 0..99 stops the crowd at exactly j (tried j = 0, 1, 2, 10, 50, 98, 99). | FC pass 22 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): exhaustive check: raising threshold j to j+1 for every j = 0..99 stops the crowd at exactly j (no exceptions).

claims.text: This example is Granovetter's threshold model of collective behaviour.
claims.source: M. Granovetter, 'Threshold Models of Collective Behavior', American Journal of Sociology 83(6) (1978); also Easley & Kleinberg (2010) ch. 19. Citation from the brief; attribution for the fact-checker to confirm (the 0..99 riot is the paper's well-known example). | FC pass 22 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Granovetter, 'Threshold Models of Collective Behavior', AJS 83(6):1420-1443 (1978) confirmed bibliographically via search (Stanford/JSTOR listing); PDF host blocked, not opened. The 0..99 riot with the 1 replaced by a 2 is the paper's illustration (my knowledge, consistent with secondary sources). E&K ch. 19 (cascading behaviour in networks, threshold rule): placement from memory, I am not sure ch. 19 cites Granovetter by name; not shown to learners.

recall.question: 50 people with thresholds 0, 1, 2, ..., 49 (everyone sees everyone). The person whose threshold is 10 is changed to 11. How many join?
recall.why: People with thresholds 0 to 9 join one by one, bringing the count to 10. Nobody left needs only 10, so the chain stops at 10.
